video_title: Matt Hougan: Solana Could Be Dramatically Undervalued | CIO of Bitwise at Breakpoint 2026 in London
gist: At Solana Breakpoint 2026, Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan attributes the recent crypto sell-off to a macro liquidity shock (hot CPI, Fed hike pricing) and argues Solana is dramatically undervalued: Bitwise's model has Solana taking 10% of global stock trading via tokenization at ~1 cent per trade for ~$7-8B revenue and a ~$300B valuation within 5 years. He contrasts Solana's revenue model with Ethereum's store-of-value pivot and notes sticky, flat BSOL ETF flows despite the drawdown.

themes.theme: Macro liquidity shock behind the crypto pullback

insights.claim: The recent crypto sell-off was driven by a macro liquidity shock — a hot CPI print reset inflation expectations and markets began pricing multiple Fed rate hikes for next year — not by anything crypto-specific.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Treat rate-hike repricing as the main driver of crypto drawdowns; watch inflation prints and Fed pricing rather than crypto news for timing.
insights.quote: We had people starting to price in multiple Fed rate hikes next year, and that is always and forever negative for crypto.

insights.claim: Hougan calls the recent hit the largest liquidity shock to finance in five or six years, largely overlooked amid Nvidia news and the Blue Wave election.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: A macro shock masked by other headlines can create dislocations; check whether liquidity conditions have stabilized.
insights.quote: we had the largest liquidity shock to hit finance in five or six years

insights.claim: Hougan believes the liquidity squeeze has played out and is probably overdone, and is cautiously optimistic the crypto bottom holds with prices higher in coming months.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: A tactical buy-the-dip signal from a major crypto CIO; the invalidation is a new low below the recent bottom.
insights.quote: I think the liquidity squeeze has now played out. I think it's probably overdone

themes.theme: Shift from momentum to fundamental crypto investing

insights.claim: With crypto fundamentals (institutional adoption, real use cases) running ahead of price, investor fatigue is an opportunity; crypto investors must switch from momentum to fundamental investing with multi-year horizons.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Position for fundamentals-ahead-of-price setups and size for multi-year holds rather than short-term momentum.
insights.quote: whenever the fundamentals are ahead of price, that's an opportunity for investors

insights.claim: Hougan expects this bull cycle to be 'a staircase up with periodic elevators down': catalysts are slow (individual wealth advisors allocating, gradual flows onto tokenized stock platforms), while most one-day events will be negative.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Don't wait for a single Schelling-point catalyst (ETF approval, Clarity Act); expect grinding gains punctuated by sharp drawdowns that are buyable.
insights.quote: this bull market cycle is going to be a staircase up with periodic elevators down

insights.claim: Hougan frames crypto as a beach ball pushed underwater: it wants to rise, and negative events like the recent liquidity shock temporarily push it down before it floats back up.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Treat negative macro shocks as temporary displacements in an underlying uptrend.

insights.claim: Solana is described as having just exited 'beta' into mainnet 1.0, which Hougan likens to around 1996 in the internet boom — very early in the real market opportunity.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Frames the investment horizon as early-cycle; patience is required despite current price frustration.
insights.quote: This is 1996 or something like that.

insights.claim: Hougan argues now is the time to build in crypto: the technology works, throughput is extraordinarily high, and regulations are in place.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Builder activity during price weakness can be a leading indicator of the next leg of on-chain growth.
insights.quote: Everything is coalesced for this to be the moment to build something really large.

insights.claim: Tokenized stocks are up about 500% year over year but only about $33 billion trades today versus roughly $300 trillion of global stock trading — a ~10,000x runway.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Tokenization is in its earliest innings; even 100x volume growth would only reach ~1% penetration, so value capture is a multi-year story.
insights.quote: Literally, there's about $33 billion of tokenized stock trading today. Globally, stocks trade $300 trillion.

insights.claim: Hougan warns that even a 10x increase in tokenized stock volume next year would leave the market only 1/1000 of the way to full penetration, so investors may be frustrated by how long the payoff takes.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Expect a mismatch between impressive growth rates and modest absolute impact; avoid short-dated bets on tokenization.

insights.claim: Tokenization ports traditional assets from 9:30–4:00, weekday-only market structure onto blockchains that trade 24/7, settle in a second, and serve as borrowable collateral.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: The value proposition is composability and collateral utility, which favors chains and venues that combine trading with lending.

insights.claim: Hougan says the theme for this cycle is the convergence of finance — stocks, bonds, commodities, futures, options and betting — into single on-chain applications where users hedge across exposures and use each as collateral; DATs, prediction markets and tokenization are all one theme.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Favor platforms and chains positioned as all-in-one on-chain super-apps for multi-asset trading and collateral.
insights.quote: The theme for this cycle is they're all coming together into one lane.

insights.claim: Breakpoint 2026 featured Zelle on stage, talks on tokenized stocks and tokenized IPOs, and Backpack launching derivatives in the US — evidence Solana is shedding its meme-coin image for an institutional one.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Track TradFi partnerships and US derivatives launches on Solana as signals of institutional adoption.

insights.claim: Traditional finance institutions such as Barclays, MasterCard and BNY were at least as represented as crypto-native firms at Breakpoint, likely more skewed to TradFi.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Institutional engagement with Solana is broadening; watch for these firms' production deployments on-chain.

insights.claim: Bitwise's Solana valuation rests on three inputs: size of the target market (all stock trading), Solana's share (10%), and its take rate (~1 cent per tokenized stock trade, currently ~1.2 cents).
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Monitor these three variables — tokenized volume, Solana share, fee per trade — to track the thesis.
insights.quote: There are only three things you need to know in terms of how to value Solana.

insights.claim: In Bitwise's base case, Solana capturing ~10% of global stock trading volume yields roughly $7–8 billion of revenue; at a 50x multiple that implies about a $300 billion chain within ~5 years.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Implies large upside from current levels if tokenized stock trading scales; the 50x multiple is benchmarked to high-growth fintechs.
insights.quote: Throw multiple on that of 50 and you end up with a $300 billion chain.

insights.claim: Hougan says Solana is dramatically undervalued today, but the re-rating will play out over five years, not five days.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: A long-horizon accumulation thesis, not a short-term trade.
insights.quote: I think it's dramatically undervalued where it is today, but that's going to play out not over the next 5 days, but over the next 5 years.

insights.claim: Solana holds about 42–43% of tokenized stock trading volume, is the clear leader with the number two spot fragmented, and Hougan expects its share to rise to around 50%.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Solana's leading share in tokenized equities is a key metric to track versus Ethereum and other L1s.
insights.quote: Right now, it has about 42 43% share of tokenized stock trading volume.

insights.claim: Solana's competitors for tokenization include Ethereum, Avalanche, Stellar and new chains, and large financial entities may not want Solana to win, which is why Bitwise models only 10% market share over 5–10 years.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Competition risk is real; the conservative-share assumption is the margin of safety in the model.

insights.claim: Bitwise's bear case assumes tokenization remains more promise than reality, and its bull case assumes Solana takes a larger share; Hougan stresses the future is unknowable but calls the base-case assumptions defensible.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Size positions acknowledging a bear case where tokenization stalls.

themes.theme: Solana vs Ethereum: revenue vs monetary premium

insights.claim: Hougan argues Solana and Ethereum now run on different valuation models: Solana is revenue-driven with a go-to-market centered on tokenization, while Ethereum has de-prioritized revenue to pursue a store-of-value/monetary-premium thesis.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Value SOL on fee revenue multiples and ETH on monetary premium; they are diverging rather than directly competing assets.
insights.quote: Solana is a revenue driven asset with a go-to-market focused on being the center of the tokenized world.

insights.claim: Ethereum's shift toward store of value stems partly from the L2 build-out reducing main-chain revenue, making a multi-hundred-billion valuation hard to justify on current revenues.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Explains weak ETH fee capture; watch whether the store-of-value narrative gains traction.

insights.claim: Hougan expects some Ethereum investors who hoped for a revenue focus to exit the asset, so ETH may struggle through an adjustment period, though it has a good shot as a secondary digital store of value alongside Bitcoin, as silver is to gold.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Possible near-term ETH holder rotation; long-term store-of-value optionality remains.
insights.quote: They're probably going to step out of the asset.

insights.claim: Solana pioneered reliably low transaction costs; spiking fees from a penny to $200 on other chains 'killed' the last bull cycle, though Hougan concedes other blockchains have since caught up on low costs.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Low fees are now table stakes, so Solana's edge must come from throughput, community focus and tokenization share.

themes.theme: ETF flows and institutional allocator behavior

insights.claim: Bitwise's Solana ETF (BSOL) has had roughly flat net flows this year despite a large price decline, and has been more stable than Bitcoin ETFs, which saw small outflows.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Sticky ETF holders reduce forced-selling risk during drawdowns.
insights.quote: We've seen no outflows and the reason is that they are making a five or 10-year bet on crypto.

insights.claim: ETF crypto holders act as 'diamond hands' because the career stigma of allocating to crypto in wealth advisory means only advisors 80–90% convinced invest; this should persist until the stigma fully lifts.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Expect ETF flows to be stickier than in equities; watch for stigma removal, which could bring larger but less committed flows.
insights.quote: They have to be 80 or 90% sure.

insights.claim: Wealth advisors typically make two crypto bets: Bitcoin as a long-term store of value and debasement hedge, and stablecoins/tokenization, often expressed via a Solana ETF allocation.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Solana is being positioned in advisor portfolios as the tokenization proxy alongside Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Institutional allocators are not worried by 20–50% drawdowns; their questions focus on what Democrats will do in Congress, quantum risk, valuation methods and revenue drivers.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Political shifts (Blue Wave) and quantum risk are the key concerns to monitor for institutional demand.

insights.claim: BSOL stakes 100% of its Solana using Bitwise's own staking infrastructure run by Helius, so holders capture priority and ordering fee upside like self-custodied stakers.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Staked ETFs deliver total return including staking yield, making them competitive with direct holding.

insights.claim: Bitwise is evolving from bringing traditional investors into crypto toward being an on-chain asset manager, including launching Jupiter Vaults with partner Jupiter.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: TradFi asset managers moving on-chain support DeFi protocols as distribution partners.

insights.claim: Across the 10 largest crypto hacks in history, the market rose in five cases and fell in five over the following 30 days, suggesting investors have not priced hacks as systemic.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Don't sell crypto broadly on exchange-hack headlines; historical evidence shows no consistent negative 30-day effect.
insights.quote: in five of those examples the market went up, in five of those examples the market went down

insights.claim: Hougan says the recent Binance hack targeted hot wallets, Binance made users whole, and hacks are platform failures not failures of crypto itself — though in the AI era the industry must raise its security game.
insights.speaker: Matt Hougan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Platform hack risk is idiosyncratic; AI-driven attack risk argues for favoring custodians with strong security.
